guide.summary: A small device that warms its own cell while it is On.
guide.biology: An aquarium heater warms the water around it, and the warmth spreads out and fades with distance.
guide.rules: A heater is a device on one open water, gel or sediment cell. It starts Off. While On it raises the warmth of its cell by 0.01 per second; warmth spreads to neighbouring cells, relaxes back toward the dish's warmth and stays between 0 and 1. Warmth is an index, not food or material: heat makes nothing. Heaters and coolers near each other add up. One furnishing or device per cell, and at most 256 furnishings and devices in a dish. Removing it adds and removes no material. No additional modeled reaction.
guide.example: Turn on a heater at one side of the dish and compare the organisms near it with those across the dish.
